one_month_reasoning: Window to 2026-10-31: (1) Barber Lake rent commencement guided for October and further Black Pearl halls going rack-ready - expected and largely priced, mild positive if confirmed; (2) FOMC on 2026-10-28 - Polymarket ($22.1M vol, 2026-10-02) prices 75% hold / 25% +25bp; a hold is mildly supportive for this rate-sensitive, levered name after the September yield-driven selloff, a hike is a clear negative; (3) Q3 results most likely land in the first week of November (Q2 was Aug 4, Q3-2025 was Nov 3), so probably just outside the window; (4) possible new lease/Apollo news is a right-tail event, while continued insider/Bitfury-holding selling and cost-overrun worries are a drag. Stock fell 6 straight days into 9/30, giving a small reversal tilt. Net: near-symmetric lognormal centered ~$15.55 (slight upward drift) with ~30% monthly sigma (112% annual vol / 3.5 = 32%).

fair_value.method: Blend of a contracted-lease DCF plus probability-weighted pipeline (8.5% WACC, 2028 NOI $800M growing 2.5%, $100M overhead, 400 MW pipeline at $4M/MW NPV) = $13.5 (60%) and a private-market cap-rate NAV (6.75% cap on $800M NOI, less overhead, plus pipeline, less $5.2B net debt) = $16.4 (40%), on 455M diluted shares.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Unlevered FCF 2028-2041 from contracted 700 MW: NOI $800M (2028) +2.5%/yr, overhead $100M +3%/yr, maint. capex 3% of NOI, cash tax 0% to 2030 then 8% of EBITDA; WACC 8.5%; TV 2041 at 2% growth with 10% re-leasing haircut -> contracted EV $9.74B; + pipeline $1.6B; - net debt $5.2B; / 455M sh = $13.5 (contracted-only $10.0; WACC 8.0% -> $15.1, 9.0% -> $12.1).

inputs_detail.value: 700 MW HPC (Barber Lake 300 MW Fluidstack/AI lab; Black Pearl 300 MW gross AWS; Stingray AWS 70 MW IT) + 207 MW Odessa mining
$11.4B over base terms, ~$793M avg annual NOI (pre-extension); Barber Lake extension adds ~$5.2B for years 11-20

inputs_detail.derivation: All halls rack-ready by Feb-2027 (Black Pearl) and Q1-2027 (Barber Lake) per DCD/QuiverQuant; ~$793M average contracted NOI and $892M 2035 NOI per Northwise imply ~2.5-3% escalators (Stingray 3% escalator per Blockspace); $800M for 2028 is the average NOI rolled forward with a partial Stingray contribution.
Q2-26 comp $42.4M + G&A $16.5M less SBC $30.5M = $28.4M/qtr (~$114M/yr); assume mining margin (~$10M/qtr gross profit) winds down and some cost discipline -> $100M.

Leases are NNN/turnkey-style with hyperscale tenants supplying IT; landlord capex limited to shell/MEP upkeep; 3% is a conservative reserve consistent with NNN data-center structure described by CREFC/MaxLife.
Accumulated deficit $1.39B plus bonus depreciation on ~$6B of new PP&E shields income for several years; 8% of EBITDA approximates 21% on EBIT after depreciation and interest.

10-yr UST ~4.75% (24/7 Wall St); project notes coupons 6.125% (Black Pearl) and 7.125% (Cipher Compute) per Northwise; ~60% debt at ~6.5% plus 40% equity at ~12% (rf 4.75% + ~1.3 beta x 5.5% ERP) = ~8.6%; cross-checked against rating-agency data-center cap rates 7.5-8.5% (CREFC). Polymarket prices further Fed hikes (Dec hike likely), so no rate relief assumed.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Private-market NAV: $800M NOI / 6.75% cap = $11.85B - $0.8B capitalized overhead + $1.6B pipeline - $5.2B net debt = $7.45B / 455M sh = $16.4.

inputs_detail.derivation: Core hyperscale NNN trades 5.0-6.5% (MaxLife citing JLL Q1-26); rating agencies use 7.0-10.0% (CREFC). AWS-leased sites ~6.25%, Barber Lake (Fluidstack, Google backstop only partial, $18B-valued private neocloud) ~7.5%; West Texas location and unstabilized status -> 6.75% blend.
Cash overhead from Q2-26 P&L capitalized at a discount multiple to reflect it scaling with the platform.

bear.story: Barber Lake overruns exceed the $359M Cipher-borne layer and/or halls slip into mid-2027; Fluidstack/AI-lab credit or AI-capex sentiment cracks further; Fed keeps hiking (10-yr >5%); pipeline stalls without tenants, forcing equity raises near lows; stock trades toward contracted-only value at a 9%+ discount rate less dilution (~$7).

base.story: Black Pearl fully delivered by Feb-2027, Barber Lake by Q1-2027, Stingray on track; run-rate NOI approaches ~$700-800M; one modest new lease or Apollo progress; rates roughly flat. Stock trades near blended NAV ($14-17).

bull.story: Signs 0.5-1 GW of new hyperscale leases (Apollo/Ulysses/2.5 GW gas campus) at >$1.2M NOI/MW with project financing, AI-infrastructure trade re-rates and rates stabilize; stock moves toward sell-side consensus (~$29).

thesis_break_reason: $8 is below the contracted-only DCF even at a 9% WACC (~$8.5) with zero pipeline value: trading there would imply the market is impairing the AWS/Fluidstack leases themselves (major construction failure, tenant default/renegotiation, or a financing squeeze/dilutive raise), not ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Lane: alternative. Basic facts from the Q2-26 8-K: $25M revenue, Adj. EBITDA -$30M, $5.54B borrowings, $832M cash + $3.73B restricted construction cash, 414M shares, $632M warrant liability. Contracted 700 MW HPC (AWS at Black Pearl/Stingray, Fluidstack then an AI lab at Barber Lake, now 20 yrs) worth ~$793M avg NOI. Alternative signals: Stocktwits retail sentiment neutral-to-cautiously-bearish and a vocal view that the Barber Lake extension was undersold; QuiverQuant shows 12 insider sales/0 buys in 6 months (incl. ~$78.5M by a Bitfury-linked holder) but large 13F adds (Morgan Stanley, T. Rowe); independent newsletters split - Mancini (Sell, FV $15, stock 'already knows' the 2.5 GW plan), Northwise (asset value vs dilution is the debate), Miner Weekly (AI-pivot index -42% from June peak); Polymarket prices Fed hikes, not cuts, consistent with the yield-driven September selloff (10-yr 4.7-4.8%); Cipher's Greenhouse board shows only 4 open roles (lean hiring, not a build-out surge, though builds are contractor-led); bitcoin odds (Polymarket) are now nearly irrelevant as mining is a small residual. Reddit and X block fetching, so those were read only via previews. Valuation: contracted-only DCF ~$10/sh at 8.5% WACC; adding a probability-weighted pipeline gives $13.5; private-market cap-rate NAV gives $16.4; blend $14.7, ~5% below the $15.46 close, so no strong valuation edge. Sell-side consensus $28.9 (MarketBeat) looks stale relative to rates and is treated only as the bull-case anchor. Distribution: lognormal-like, median ~$15.0, sigma ~0.78 (below the 112% realized vol, which was inflated by the business-model pivot, but still wide given ~43% net-debt-to-EV leverage), skewed so the bull tail (new leases) is fatter than the asset-backed left tail. Scenario mean ~$16.5 vs median ~$15.
